meta_desc: Inventory, orders, invoices and schedule for all your job sites in one place, with an agent that checks everything overnight, sees shortages coming, gets quotes and waits for your OK. Join the waitlist.
og_desc: While the site sleeps, Plumo checks. Join the waitlist.
hero_lead: Inventory, orders, invoices and schedule for every job site in one place, with an advisor that lets nothing slip. It sees a shortage coming before the crew stops, catches the double order and the material that walks off, and waits for your OK in the morning.
nota_pe: Free to join. We'll email you when a spot opens.

mad_h2: Overnight, one sum at a time.
mad_lead: Today the job lives scattered across spreadsheets, WhatsApp groups and somebody's head, and money slips through the cracks in between. Plumo pulls it together and checks it every night, showing where each number came from.
e1_p: Compares what each work front needs with what's in the storeroom and what's already on the way, before the crew is left standing.
e2_p: If another site has leftovers of the same material, a transfer comes first. Buying is the last resort.
e3_p: Asks your suppliers for prices, compares them with your last purchase and with reference costs, and picks the best offer.
e4_p: Nothing is bought, paid or rescheduled without a person's OK. And anything approved can be undone.
tras_h2: Behind the scenes, the agent stitches together everything the job already has.
tras_lead: Storeroom, orders, invoices, schedule, quotes: what lives in five places today ends up in one. The agent cross-checks it all, looks up prices online, asks the rules for the math and hands you a ready proposal. Every thread is a real lookup.
palco_aria: Animated example: the agent checking the job's sources to put together a proposal

p_prop_s: nothing is bought without your OK
p_web_s: price and lead time near you

cost_h2: One site's leftovers are another site's shortage.
cost_lead: Rebar, cement and block forgotten in a corner of one site turn into a double order at the next: idle money nobody sees, because nobody looks at both at once. Plumo does, and stitches the transfer together.
cost_aria: Example: moving rebar between two sites
cost_title: Galpão Ipê has 12 spare 10 mm rebars and Casa Jatobá needs 12. The agent stitches the transfer along the seam between them.
c_prop_s: Galpão Ipê → Casa Jatobá · saves a $1,140 purchase
cant_h2: Foremen don't open apps. They send voice notes.
cant_lead1: The site talks to Plumo over the WhatsApp it already uses: voice notes, a photo of the invoice, a photo of the pallet. The agent turns that into records, checks it against the order and only asks what it has to.
cant_lead2: Nobody fills in forms with mortar on their hands, and a short delivery gets caught the same day, not at month-end.

manha_h2: In the morning, the decision is ready.
manha_lead: Open Plumo in the truck or at the office and see only what needs you, in order of deadline. Approve with one tap and see right away what you stopped losing. Everything is logged with who, when and why.

prot_vazio: approve to see what stops slipping away
ciclo_h2: From shortage to leftovers, one thread.
ciclo_lead: Money slips away between the purchase and the site: short deliveries paid in full, double orders, forgotten leftovers, material that walks off. Plumo follows every material from forecast to leftovers, and never lets go halfway.
pr1: Inventory, purchasing, invoices, schedule and the site itself, across all your jobs, with an advisor that reviews it all every night.
pr2: Buying, paying and rescheduling all need the OK of someone on your team.
pr3: Every approval is logged with who, when and the math that justified it.
pr4_b: The system does the math, not the AI.
pr4: Stock and shortages come from rules; the agent only quotes the result.
lista_lead: What does a day of crew standing around waiting for cement cost you? Or the invoice that came short and got paid in full? We're opening gradually, for small and mid-size builders and for owner-builders. Tell us a bit about you and we'll let you know when it's your turn.
f1_a: We haven't set pricing yet. People on the list hear first and get founder terms.
f2_q: Do I have to replace my spreadsheet or ERP?
f2_a: No. The idea is to start alongside what you already use and bring the data over gradually.
f3_q: Does the agent buy on its own?
f3_a: Never. It prepares the quote, order or transfer and waits for someone on your team to approve it.
f4_q: Do I pay for the AI separately?
f4_a: Your choice: use your own Anthropic key or platform credits, with usage shown per site.
f5_q: What do you do with my email?
f5_a: We only use it to tell you about Plumo. We don't share it, and you can leave the list anytime.
rodape: Keep every site plumb. Made in Brazil.
